explanation: A mass warps the space around it into a gravitational field g — the acceleration a test object would feel at each point, pointing straight toward the source. The arrows show this field: they all aim inward, and their length shrinks with the square of distance, so the inner ring's field is far stronger than the outer ring's. Slide M to scale the whole field up or down (more mass, stronger pull everywhere), and watch the orbiting test mass report g = G*M/r^2 in m/s^2 at its current radius.
bullets: g is the force per kilogram a test mass feels — it points toward the source.
Inverse-square: g falls off as 1/r^2, so the field weakens fast with distance.
g = G*M/r^2 depends only on the SOURCE mass M, not the test mass.
